answer: Epoch-Bridge Anchor Rule (a cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule): at each epoch’s dawn, agents commit to a compact behavioural anchor—timing, action n-grams, resource profile—linked by a consistency proof to the prior epoch. Random cross-epoch challenges replay sampled trajectories; deviation beyond tolerance quarantines the identity and forfeits rewards. An attacker must keep every sybil running across epochs with distinct coherent histories, paying persistent compute/state and correlation risk; fresh identities cannot bridge in at use time.
